derivation: Synthetic tape, ATR_START=10. price(t) = 100 - t/6 for t<=60 (so price(60)=90.0 exactly), price(t) = 90 + 0.5*(t-60) after. Completed 1s bars [t,t+1] carry ts_init=(t+1)s. The bearish 1m regime starts at t=0; the bullish flip at t=60 is dispatched after the 1s bar closing at 60, so the completed prior (bearish) regime's LOW is price(60)=90.0 and that low is the structural origin of the bullish regime. Definition: structural_max_expansion_checkpoint_atr = direction * (favourable extreme - origin) / checkpoint_atr, where the favourable extreme of the bullish regime at epoch T is the highest completed-1s high <= T = price(T). The value is unavailable (null) until a completed PRIOR 5m regime exists: the 5m bar closing at 300 opens the first 5m regime (direction -1), the bar closing at 600 flips it (direction +1) and completes the prior one. Snapshot T=360s: no completed prior 5m regime -> null. Snapshot T=660s, family_a_atr (checkpoint_atr)=15: extreme=price(660)=390, origin=90 -> 300/15 = 20.0 (the frozen-ATR sibling would read 300/10 = 30.0, which is the contrast this feature exists for). Snapshot T=720s, family_a_atr=12: extreme=price(720)=420 -> 330/12 = 27.5. The tape continues to ts_init=726s so the availability guard is exercised after the last snapshot.
